documents.title: Academic Affairs Guidance for Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools
documents.stance_why: The principles say "Faculty should decide whether and how generative AI is used in courses", so the university sets no uniform stance, though it states a fallback of "permitted but must be disclosed" when a syllabus is silent.
documents.summary: Short university guidance stating that users must follow law and local rules, disclose AI use and own AI-produced content. Faculty decide course rules; absent a statement, AI is permitted with disclosure.

units.why: The statement says AI is "a valuable, dynamic, and vital tool", a benefit claim with no rule attached, so it is P87 (benefits) rather than P44 (career skill); informs, neutral.
units.anchor: Artificial Intelligence is a valuable, dynamic, and vital tool.

units.why: "you must abide by all applicable laws and policies when you use AI" binds everyone to existing law and policy, which is P77.
units.anchor: you must abide by all applicable laws and policies when you use AI

units.why: "you should strive to use AI ethically" is a general ethical-use call with no specific content, P116.
units.anchor: you should strive to use AI ethically

units.why: "follow guidelines (including prohibitions) provided by your dean, instructor, supervisor" makes the local authority set the rule, so P04 (who decides); chosen over P78 because the focus is on others setting rules.
units.anchor: You should follow guidelines (including prohibitions) provided by your dean, instructor, supervisor

units.why: "You should disclose the use of AI in an appropriate way" asks all users to disclose AI use, P24.
units.anchor: You should disclose the use of AI in an appropriate way.

units.why: "exercise sound judgment" is a general expectation of responsible use with no specific content, P116.
units.anchor: You should exercise sound judgment in your use of AI.

units.why: AI use must be "consistent with university policies on confidentiality and privacy", a privacy rule (P50) rather than a generic law rule.
units.anchor: consistent with university policies on confidentiality and privacy

units.why: "You are the author of content that you produce with AI and responsible for its accuracy" makes users own what they produce, P29; accuracy responsibility is partly P31 but ownership is the main point.

units.anchor: Faculty should clearly communicate expectations to students.

units.fit_note: Specifically asks instructors to define what counts as academic dishonesty, not only AI permissions.
